newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi shares dip on weak demand, turnover down.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi shares dip on weak demand, turnover down.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index shed 6.27 points to 3374.30 as several key shares across the board eased, bourse officials and brokers said.
They told Reuters on Monday that turnover was posted at 17.6 million shillings on 415,458 shares versus 17.3 million shillings on 330,668 shares on Friday.

"If you look on the special boards -- three-day offer board and one-hour hold board, you'll see there's definitely a lot of supply but no demand," a senior broker said. At least three million shares are on offer on the three-day board.
Sasini Tea & Coffee gained a shilling to close at 77 while Rea Vipingo was unchanged at 9.
Kenya Airways gained 20 cents to close at 8.70 while Uchumi Supermarkets eased to 40.25 from 41.
Barclays Bank closed at 116 from 115 while Kenya Commercial Bank was unchanged at 94.
Standard Chartered Bank fell 46 from 46.50 while National Bank of Kenya closed at 16.30 from 15.50.

Some brokers said the market had simply taken a breather after last week's high turnover which was boosted by the introduction on the market of Tourism Promotion Services (TPS), the trading name for Serena Lodges & Hotels.
Kenya Power & Lighting gained 3.0 to close at 139 while Total Kenya was unchanged at 66. British American Tobacco eased to 60.50 from 61.

The CBK bond traded 400,000 shillings at 103.5875 percent from Friday's close of 103.4165 percent, while the East African Development Bank corporate bond traded five million shillings of bonds at 100.48 percent from 99.67 percent.
